title: Sephiria Builds: Weapon Paths and Artifact Pairings
description: Plan a Sephiria run around a weapon path and Artifact family, including the Companion summoner route. Compare community-reported setups, practical pairing ideas, and patch changes.
meta: Updated 30 October 2026, including the 1.1.0 workshop beta. Community build notes carry explicit version limits; check current item and upgrade descriptions in-game.
body:
Plan a Sephiria run around a weapon path and one or two Artifact families. The combinations below are community reports, not official loadouts or a ranked tier list; item offers and patch changes can change the result.

The summoner route is the Companion build: Companion-tagged pets, Ballista, and Tablets on summons.

What actually makes a build work

  • Choose a weapon evolution and a combo family that support each other, then focus your Artifact picks around that plan.
  • Check the Journal before a run for unlocked weapon paths, Artifact effects, and combo tags.
  • After an Anvil or Tablet choice, check the live item description and whether its effect actually supports your route.
  • Use the Wishing Fountain for available pre-run Artifacts, but avoid making the whole plan depend on a Bond Artifact: Steam players report that Bond Artifacts are not offered there.

Community-reported setup names

The first seven names and paths below are retained from earlier community build references. Their current-version routes and claimed performance have not been independently verified; treat them as search leads and confirm each evolution in your Journal.

Steam discussion routes to compare

Run directionWeapon and Artifact pairing reportedDecision point
Companion / summonerA player report pairs Companion summons, including a Lightning Ballista interaction, with Sword & Shield guarding and MP recovery.Guarding consumes MP; only commit if your current run can sustain it. Treat reported clears as anecdotes.
Storm CloudA Steam player recommends the Long Sword path; another describes Storm Cloud with Magitech support.Try this if you want damage to continue while you reposition; inspect the current combo tags and Tablet effects.
Solar BladePlayers recommend building around Solar Blade activations; Meteorite Earring is mentioned as a key Artifact.Official 1.0.31 added Midday Whetstone and Meteorite Mirror; 1.0.33 fixed Solar Blade retrieval interactions. Compare current Journal descriptions.
Sword & Shield: Blinding SilenceOfficial 1.0.31 upgrade: pair Blinding Silence with Thunder's Earring.Using Special Attack: Cleave immediately activates Thunder's Earring; the upgrade also increases Lightning Damage and the artifact's attacks.
Sword & Shield: Garden of Needle IceOfficial 1.0.31 upgrade: pair Garden of Needle Ice with Ice Vine.When activated, Ice Vine orbits the player and no longer has a cooldown; the upgrade also increases Cold Damage.
Frost RelicCommunity reports describe Oracle's Staff / Voluspa, Blizzard's Eve / Hammer, and Drifa Dagger / Compass placements.Check which trigger route matches your unlocked weapon and available Artifact pool.
Crossbow GlacierA Steam player reports Frost Veil with Glacier, Wind Song, and reload-supporting Crossbow Artifacts.Use as a player route to test, not a guaranteed freeze setup.
Blizzard Scythe (legacy report)An earlier community page reports a Dagger → Dormant Frost → Drifa route that evolves into Blizzard Scythe.This path is retained from the existing video reference, not independently confirmed in current Steam notes; verify labels and unlocks in your Journal.

Artifact and Tablet pairings

Use the combo labels and Tablet effects visible in your current inventory to decide where an upgrade applies. Community discussions point to several broad pairings: Storm Cloud with Magitech, Solar Blade with Ember support, and Frost Relic with Lake-series effects. Exact placement, costs, and set thresholds should be checked against the current client.

Version correction: old community advice describes Sword & Shield's Starlight as a reflect build. Official 1.0.31 notes changed Starlight so its counterattack uses Riposte Blade Fragment, launching toward the nearest enemy and piercing enemies in its path. Do not use the old reflect description as a current build recipe.

Costumes and Talents

Costumes change starting stats; choose one that supports the weapon route you want to practice. Talent access and reset notes are on the Destiny Inscription page. For the town Artifact picker, see Wishing Fountain.

What the 1.1.0 beta changes for builds

The 1.1.0 update entered public beta on 29 October 2026 (Steam branch workshop-beta). It is a beta — anything in it may change before the official release — but three parts matter for build planning:

  • Greatsword gains a new upgrade, Scattered Longing. Normal Attack builds Chain Slash stacks; Special Attack during the 2nd hit performs Double Slash; at 10 stacks the final hit becomes Space Slash (Physical 400% plus lingering damage). If it survives the beta, the Greatsword route gets a real combo engine.
  • Two new Artifacts (Wagner's Glass Bottle, Compass of Breakthrough), two new Tablets (Growth, Reverberation), and a new Grimoire (Ice Storm) — grid-adjacency planning on the Artifacts and Tablets page gets new options.
  • Riposte Staff Fragment was re-valued (counter damage roughly halved at each rarity) and Distribution can now be rotated — existing guard/counter and grid routes need re-checking against the beta client.

Run History (unlocked via Destiny Inscription, last 100 runs) also ships in this beta — useful for comparing your own routes instead of relying on montage videos.

Version notes

Steam's official update feed checked for this guide includes 1.0.33 (September 2026) and the 1.1.0 workshop beta (29 October 2026). The 1.0.31 update added weapon upgrades and Artifacts and changed several existing effects; 1.0.33 then corrected Solar Blade interactions and changed Master's Tsuba. Community setup posts linked below are dated August 2026 and may predate those changes. Verify all item names and effects in your current Journal before relying on a named route.
